title: Refinement Exchange Coherence
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring. Use $D(\mathcal T_T)$ for strict towers of constant $B$-module sheaves on the small pro-etale site of each scheme $T$, with the operations $G_u,R_u^{\mathcal T},J_j$ of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. For every commutative square with proper verticals and quasi-compact open horizontals use the normalized comparison $\gamma_Q$ and open base-change map $\beta$ of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. All direct-image and open-extension composition identifications are canonical.
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type and let $c_i=(j_i:X\hookrightarrow\overline X_i,p_i:\overline X_i\to Y)$ be supplied compactifications [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$ (a proper $Y$-map with $uj_1=j_2$), let $Q_u$ have top $j_1$, bottom $j_2$, left $1_X$, right $u$. Put $F_i=R_{p_i}^{\mathcal T}J_{j_i}$ and
$$C_u=R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\gamma_{Q_u}:F_2\longrightarrow F_1.$$
Restrict to $M\in D(\mathcal T_X)$ whose evaluations are restrictions of scalars along maps $B\to\Lambda_n$, with $\Lambda_n$ finite commutative, of $\nu_X^*L_n$ for $L_n\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_n)$ [def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport]. Then $C_u$ is an isomorphism. For every base change $g:Y'\to Y$ put $e_i=(R_{p_i'}^{\mathcal T}\beta_{j_i,g})E_{p_i}^{\mathcal T}:G_gF_i\to F_i'G_{g'}$, where $E$ is the proper pullback-square mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. In the derived strict-tower category itself,
$$C'_u e_2=e_1G_gC_u,\qquad C_{\mathrm{id}}=1,\qquad C_{v\circ u}=C_uC_v.$$
For a common refinement $d\xrightarrow{u_i}c_i$ define $I_{12}=C_{u_2}^{-1}C_{u_1}:F_1\to F_2$. These isomorphisms are independent of the common refinement and the refinement arrows, satisfy $I_{23}I_{12}=I_{13}$, and intertwine the $e_i$. No qcqs or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $Y$; compactifications are supplied.

proof.text: For a refinement u:c_1\to c_2, the equations u j_1=j_2 and p_2u=p_1 make Q_u the commutative proper/open square with top j_1, bottom j_2, left identity, and right u. The strict-tower operations and open extension therefore identify its two compactification candidates as F_i=R_{p_i}^{\mathcal T}J_{j_i}, with all direct-image and open-extension compositors canonical. Under these identifications the normalized comparison supplied by the proper/open calculus is exactly C_u=R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\gamma_{Q_u}.

proof.text: The stated hypothesis on M is exactly the finite scalar etale-origin hypothesis of the strict-tower proper/open calculus, with V=X and r=1_X. Thus gamma_{Q_u,M} is an isomorphism. Applying R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T} preserves its inverse, proving that C_u is invertible. This also applies after base change: evaluation commutes with G, scalar restriction commutes with the constant-coefficient inverse image by the inverse-image comparison of the transport definition, and the site-comparison pullback isomorphism identifies g'^*nu_X^*L_n with nu_{X'}^*g'_{et}^{-1}L_n. The latter remains bounded below: [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], applied with R=Lambda_n to g', makes etale inverse image exact, so it preserves the vanishing of cohomology below the bound for L_n. Hence G_{g'}M has the required finite scalar etale origins, without any uniform bound in n.

proof.text: Write bar g_i:overline X_i'->overline X_i for the base-change projections. The supplied primed compactifications, refinement arrow and pullback squares identify the pullback square with Q_u'. Apply the proper/open calculus base-change identity with p=u, r=1_X, k=j_1, i=j_2 and b=bar g_2; the identity mate E_{1_X} is normalized by the unit equation in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-direct-image-coherence]. Apply R_{p_2'}^{\mathcal T} to this identity and precompose with E_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}J_{j_2}. Naturality of E_{p_2} moves gamma_{Q_u} across this precomposition. The mate-pasting law for the proper maps u,p_2 identifies the resulting composite (R_{p_2'}E_u)(E_{p_2}R_u) with E_{p_2u}=E_{p_1}, using the canonical direct-image compositors from the operation definition. The two resulting paths are therefore exactly C_u' e_2 and e_1 G_g C_u. Their equality is an equality of strict-tower transformations from the cited calculus, not an inference from evaluations. In Lean the identity and horizontal-pasting normalizations for the concrete strict-tower operations are supplied explicitly by [lem-cbc-strict-tower-direct-image-coherence]; the generic mate-pasting theorem alone does not state these identifications.

proof.text: For the identity refinement, Q_u has identity vertical maps, so the identity clause of the calculus gives C_{\mathrm{id}}=1. If c_1\xrightarrow{u}c_2\xrightarrow{v}c_3 are refinements, the pasted square is Q_{v\circ u}; the vertical pasting identity for \gamma, followed by the canonical direct-image compositors, gives C_{v\circ u}=C_uC_v. These are equalities of strict-tower transformations before any evaluation. Apply the two unit equations and the associative compositor equation of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-direct-image-coherence] to include the outer proper direct image.

proof.text: First prove equality for two parallel refinement arrows: cofilteredness equalizes them after a refinement t, the composition law identifies the resulting comparisons, and cancellation of C_t gives equality. For two common-refinement objects choose a common domination. Replacing either leg by a parallel leg leaves the ratio unchanged; the composition law cancels the common domination from the two ratios. Thus the common comparison is independent of the object and of both arrows.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: 'independent of the compactification and natural by the corresponding properties of the two factors' and 'compatibility of the comparisons of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] with the completed maps'; independence of the common refinement and its arrows

proof.text: Repeatedly taking common refinements gives one d with arrows u_i:d->c_i for any three compactifications. By step 5 every I_{ij} may be computed there. Associativity and cancellation give I_{23}I_{12}=C_{u_3}^{-1}C_{u_2}C_{u_2}^{-1}C_{u_1}=I_{13}. For base change the supplied d' with arrows u_i' is a common refinement; step 2 guarantees that C_{u_i'} is invertible on G_{g'}M. The equation of step 3 for each u_i reads C_{u_i'}e_i=e_d G_g C_{u_i}. Consequently C_{u_2'} e_2 G_g I_{12}=e_d G_g(C_{u_2}I_{12})=e_d G_g C_{u_1}=C_{u_1'}e_1. Cancel C_{u_2'} to obtain e_2 G_g I_{12}=I_{12}'e_1, as required. All cancellations take place in the derived strict-tower categories.
